cap: Three male-tract questions each end in one structure. Urethral folds that fail to fuse leave a ventral opening, hypospadias; a genital tubercle formed in the wrong place gives a dorsal opening, epispadias, with bladder exstrophy. The testis follows the gubernaculum through the abdominal wall and takes a covering from each layer, so the internal oblique gives the cremaster. Undescended testes keep a raised germ cell tumor risk.
teach: Failed descent matters for three reasons: the warm abdominal or canal position impairs sperm production, germ cell tumor risk rises and persists in both testes even after orchiopexy, and the open processus vaginalis that often accompanies it allows hernia or hydrocele. Early orchiopexy improves fertility and makes the testis easy to examine, but it does not remove the cancer risk.
